title: Stop hardcoding TextDirection.rtl on TrackLabelStep's free-text field regardless of app locale
why: TrackLabelStep's TextFormField is the free-text 'name this track' input — the user can type anything, in either app locale. Forcing textDirection: TextDirection.rtl unconditionally (not gated on locale or on the defaultLabel's script) means an English-locale user typing 'Morning Bavli Study' gets a right-anchored cursor/hint and base-RTL layout for a field the rest of the (LTR) English screen doesn't otherwise use RTL for. This is precisely what the currently-broken `no_hardcoded_text_direction` custom lint rule exists to catch — with custom_lint crashing repo-wide, nothing currently flags it.
recommendation: Drive textDirection from the ambient Directionality/locale (or drop the explicit override and let Flutter's default locale-derived directionality apply), the same way other bidi-sensitive widgets in this batch (scope_views.dart's chooseLevelPrompt) key off useHebrew instead of hardcoding a direction.
acceptance_criteria: textDirection on this field is either removed or computed from Directionality.of(context)/a Hebrew-Terms-aware flag, not a literal TextDirection.rtl.
An EN-locale widget test asserts the field's effective text direction is ltr.
custom_lint's no_hardcoded_text_direction rule (once unbroken) passes on this file.
